subject: Hosted API — long-tail usage tiering and inflation safeguard
messages:
From: Nathan Li <n.li@horizonai.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: enterprise-procurement@horizonai.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — long tail usage and protections

I wanted to follow up after our POC wrap-up. Horizon is excited about the latency numbers and model quality — thanks to the team. Before we surface this to procurement, a few items they flagged that we'd like your guidance on:

- Long-tail usage: our usage profile is spiky. We anticipate a core committed tier but a non-trivial long-tail of ad-hoc bursts (est. additional 1.5b tokens/mo). How do you typically price heavy long-tail usage once the committed band is consumed?
- Price protections: procurement pushed back on open-ended escalations. They asked for a price cap tied to CPI (we suggested CPI + 2% max) and an MFN-style clause if you give better public list pricing for similar customers in the next 12 months.
- True-ups & statements: they want quarterly true-ups and visibility into token definitions (what counts as an embedding vs. generation token).

Can you share a short proposal or example tiers/guardrails we can present internally? Attaching the draft MA for reference.

Thanks,
Nathan
VP Product, Horizon AI

Attachment: Horizon_MA_proposal_v2.pdf (1 page, summary)
From: irene.choi@redwood.com <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Nathan Li <n.li@horizonai.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — long tail usage and protections

Nathan — great to hear the POC went well. Quick replies inline and a proposal sketch below. Happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

- Long-tail handling: we usually offer a 2-band structure: committed tier with a stepped-per-token rate, plus a negotiated overage rate for burst usage. Example: 5B tokens/mo committed at $0.0009/token; overage billed at $0.0015/token up to 2x committed; after that we apply surge pricing or routing to lower-cost model variants. We can also add an optional overflow bucket at a blended rate to smooth the billing unpredictability.
- CPI / price cap: we can support an annual CPI-based adjustment but prefer a floor/ceiling approach. We could do CPI capped at +2% with an absolute maximum of +3% if tied to a 12-month lock. MFN is trickier — legal typically limits MFN to public list changes and comparable customer profile thresholds.
- True-ups & token defs: quarterly true-ups are standard. We'll include a token definitions appendix and a sample billing CSV.

Proposal sketch (for internal review):
1) Commit band: 5B tokens/month — $0.0009/token (12-month term)
2) Overage: up to 2B tokens/month at $0.00135/token; beyond that overflow bucket at $0.0010/token blended (applies only if you opt into overflow smoothing)
3) Price protections: 12-month price lock from signature; annual CPI adjustment up to +2% (max +3% if CPI spikes)
4) MFN: limited to published public list rates for substantially similar customers (reconsiders every 12 months)
5) True-up: quarterly with a 30-day invoice window; definition appendix attached

I'll have Marcus pull together an official pricing sheet and a short note our legal can share on MFN language. When's a good time this week for a 30-minute call?

— Irene
Director, Strategic Sales 
Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing — long tail usage and protections

Forwarding Nathan's note — a few internal action items:

1) Pricing sheet: I'll prepare the per-tier Excel with the blended overflow option and two overage bands. Aim to keep headline around $0.0009 for the committed band to stay competitive.
2) Legal: Vivek, can you review MFN language and confirm whether we can accept a public-list MFN limited to customers >$500k ARR? Also outline acceptable CPI cap language — procurement asked for 'CPI + 2% cap' phrasing, but we need to ensure our margin assumptions hold.
3) Finance: Lauren, please run a 12-month P&L sensitivity: base commit vs 30% overage scenarios and a CPI +3% case. We need to know if we can support the overflow blended at $0.0010.

I'll attach the draft pricing sheet once done.

-Marcus
Head of Sales Ops
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API pricing — long tail usage and protections

Quick legal read:

- MFN: we can accept an MFN clause restricted to publicly posted list price changes and to customers with materially similar usage profile (we should define the threshold; $500k ARR or >10B tokens/yr is reasonable). We should avoid open MFN that covers discounts tied to channel/non-public arrangements.
- CPI / cap: CPI-linked adjustments are fine but must be bounded. Proposed: annual adjustment = min(CPI, +2%); absolute cap of +3% for extraordinary inflation events, with carve-outs for materially increased cloud input costs if supported by third-party index.
- Term: price lock for 12 months from signature; thereafter annual adjustments per the CPI formula.
- Audit: grant procurement the right to a single annual compliance audit on billing definitions and sample logs, subject to an NDA and qualified auditor list.

I'll draft language for inclusion in the MA and share redline tomorrow.

Vivek
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Nathan Li <n.li@horizonai.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: enterprise-procurement@horizonai.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — long tail usage and protections

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement liked the two-band approach and the overflow smoothing idea. A couple of follow-ups before we route to legal:

- Could you confirm the blended overflow example with numbers (committed 5B @ $0.0009; overage 0–2B @ $0.00135; overflow bucket blended at $0.0010) and the monthly invoice math? Procurement wants a worked sample showing three scenarios: (a) steady usage at commit; (b) commit + 50% overage; (c) commit + 200% overage in a given month.
- For MFN, they requested the public-list restriction you mentioned, but also asked for a 30-day notice if Redwood changes public list pricing so they have time to exercise any negotiation rights. Is that feasible?
- Audit: noted and we'll prepare NDA language as needed.

If you can send the worked sample and draft MA redline by EOD Wednesday we'll try to get to legal the following week.

Best,
Nathan
VP Product, Horizon AI
